decisive_items: right bundle-branch block (RBBB) and left anterior fascicular block (LAFB)
third-degree AV block with minimum heart rate of 36 beats/min
response.rationale: Age-related progressive conduction-system fibrosis (Lev disease) best unifies the trifascicular block and progression to third-degree AV block with exertional syncope; high-degree AV block is the immediate arrhythmic manifestation, while echo excludes valvular/cardiomyopathic causes.

rejected.why: Pulmonary hypertension is mild, likely secondary, and does not explain the AV block or syncope.
Lacks typical echo/LV amyloid features (thickened walls, restrictive/low-voltage pattern) and is less parsimonious than conduction-system fibrosis.
Hypertension and LA enlargement are nonspecific; there is no LVH or diastolic evidence to account for third-degree AV block.
Exercise syncope fits classically, but this is directly contradicted by 'No significant valvular abnormality' and absence of a murmur.
LAFB is only one component of the ECG pattern and does not explain intermittent complete heart block or syncope.
Left atrial enlargement is an echo finding, not a unifying diagnosis for the conduction block and syncope.
Duplicate of the runner-up; high-degree AV block is the acute manifestation rather than the underlying sclerodegenerative diagnosis.
